bib.title: BLOOM: A 176B-Parameter Open-Access Multilingual Language Model

read.skipped: Author/contributor name lists (first ~9k chars) and the body of the reference list (skimmed for arXiv ids). Figure data (Fig 7-12) is plots and was not readable as text.

question: Can a 176B-parameter multilingual decoder-only LLM be built and released openly by a large collaboration, and how does it perform?
contributions: Release of BLOOM, a 176B-parameter open-access model trained on 46 natural and 13 programming languages (ROOTS corpus)
Documentation of the data, architecture, tokenizer, engineering and training choices
Evaluation in zero-shot, one-shot and after multitask prompted finetuning (BLOOMZ), plus embeddings, probing, bias and carbon footprint
Release under the Responsible AI License with Apache 2.0 code

method.summary: A 70-layer causal decoder-only transformer with ALiBi positions and an embedding LayerNorm, trained with Megatron-DeepSpeed on 384 A100 GPUs for about 3.5 months on ROOTS (about 341B tokens, plus 25B tokens repeated). Smaller sizes (560M to 7.1B) were also trained. BLOOMZ is BLOOM finetuned on xP3 multitask prompts.
method.task: next-token pretraining; multitask prompted finetuning; contrastive finetuning for embeddings

datasets.name: ROOTS

datasets.preprocessing: per-source quality indicators tuned per language, two near-duplicate removal steps, regex-based PII redaction on the OSCAR portion; GitHub code deduplicated for exact matches

models.name: BLOOM
models.architecture: causal decoder-only transformer, ALiBi, embedding LayerNorm, GELU, tied embeddings

models.name: BLOOMZ
models.architecture: BLOOM after multitask finetuning on xP3

models.name: OPT, GPT-J, GPT-Neo, GPT-NeoX, mGPT, T0, XGLM, M2M-100 (615M), AlexaTM, mTk-Instruct, Codex, GPT-fr

training.objective: autoregressive next-token prediction (Eq 1); multitask finetuning on xP3; contrastive finetuning (SGPT bi-encoder) for embeddings
training.lr_schedule: cosine decay over 410B tokens to a minimum of 6e-6 (176B) or 1e-5 (smaller); decay never completed because warmup + decay tokens exceeded total tokens
training.precision: bfloat16 mixed precision (gradient accumulation and softmax in float32); Table 3 lists float16 for the smaller models
training.hardware: Jean Zay: 48 nodes x 8 NVIDIA A100 80GB (384 GPUs) plus 4 spare nodes; Megatron-DeepSpeed, 3D parallelism, ZeRO stage 1
training.compute: 1,082,990 compute hours; 156 TFLOPs per GPU in fastest configuration (half of 312 peak)

other.finetune_lr: 2.0e-5 for all sizes, constant, 0 warmup tokens
other.finetune_checkpoint: best checkpoint chosen on a separate validation set; performance plateaus after 1 - 6 billion tokens
other.extra_tokens: 25B additional tokens on repeated data for the large models, after Hoffmann et al. 2022
other.embedding_layernorm: extra LayerNorm after the embedding layer, added for stability
other.failures: 1-2 GPU failures per week; one loss spike; 5-10h downtimes from a data-loader deadlock and disk space
other.table3_note: Table 3 columns merge identical entries, so which sizes share a value is read from text and layout

inference.decoding: greedy for MT and summarization, until EOS (and \n###\n in 1-shot)
inference.max_tokens: 64 for WMT14; 512 for Flores-101 and DiaBLa
inference.samples: SuperGLUE: 5 prompts per task; probing: 3 seeds; CrowS-Pairs: 8 runs; others not stated
inference.prompting: zero- and one-shot with promptsource prompts written before BLOOM was available and not refined with models; classification scored by maximum log likelihood over candidate label strings

metrics.name: BLEU (sacrebleu)
metrics.definition: BLEU+case:mixed+numrefs.1+smooth.exp+{13a,tok:spm-flores}+version:2.2.1; default tokenisation for WMT and DiaBLa, spm-flores-101 for Flores

metrics.name: ROUGE-2, ROUGE-L, Levenshtein distance
metrics.definition: ROUGE with a SentencePiece tokenizer built from Flores-101

metrics.name: fertility
metrics.definition: subwords created per word or per dataset by the tokenizer

metrics.name: weighted F1
metrics.definition: probing logistic regression, averaged over 3 seeds

metrics.name: CrowS-Pairs accuracy
metrics.definition: prompt accuracy selecting the stereotyped or non-stereotyped sentence; 50 means no preference

eval.protocol: zero/few-shot prompting; Mann-Whitney U, ANOVA and Pearson tests for probing correlations; one-sample T-test (p<.05) for CrowS-Pairs

limits: Embedding LayerNorm improved stability but penalizes zero-shot generalization (Le Scao et al. 2022); it may be unnecessary under bfloat16.
Ablations ran at 1.3B and 6.7B scale; the authors note outlier features appear above 6.7B so results may not extrapolate.
Mixture-of-experts and state-space models were not considered.
The learning-rate decay never finished because warmup + decay tokens exceeded total tokens; the last 25B tokens were repeated data.
Swahili and Yoruba, under-represented (<50k tokens), translate very poorly.
ROUGE-2 understates summary quality; CrowS-Pairs adapted from masked LMs has validity issues and covers only English and French.
Probing covers only 17 languages and averaged layers at end of training.
Prompts were not tuned, so results are realistic rather than best-case.
Carbon API figure is not representative of all deployments.
